title: Baroque & the Dramatic Light
description: The drama, movement, and shadow-pierced chiaroscuro of 17th-century Europe.
source: Art Institute of Chicago, Cleveland Museum of Art, The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Wikimedia Commons

items.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
items.description_narrative: This monumental work captures the dramatic moment when Jesus Christ calls Matthew to abandon his life as a tax collector and follow him. Caravaggio's use of intense chiaroscuro and naturalism illuminates the figures, highlighting the spiritual encounter within a seemingly everyday setting.
items.tags: religious, biblical, baroque, chiaroscuro, tenebrism, dramatic, naturalism, calling

items.title: The Supper at Emmaus
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio powerfully depicts the dramatic moment Christ reveals himself to two disciples in Emmaus, capturing their astonished reactions. The artist masterfully employs intense chiaroscuro and lifelike figures, drawing the viewer into this profound biblical scene.
items.tags: religious, baroque, chiaroscuro, realism, dramatic, biblical, italian

items.title: The Conversion of Saint Paul on the Way to Damascus
items.description_narrative: This painting dramatically captures the moment Saul, en route to Damascus, is struck by a blinding light and hears the voice of Christ, leading to his conversion into Saint Paul. Caravaggio employs intense chiaroscuro and a stark composition to heighten the spiritual and physical impact of this divine intervention.
items.tags: religious, biblical, baroque, conversion, Paul, dramatic, chiaroscuro

items.title: Bacchus
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio's Bacchus presents the Roman god of wine as a languid youth, inviting the viewer with a direct gaze and an extended glass. The detailed depiction of ripe fruit and the realistic rendering of the figure exemplify the artist's innovative approach to classical subjects.
items.tags: bacchus, mythology, baroque, tenebrism, realism, classical subject, wine, sensuality

items.title: Judith Beheading Holofernes
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio's painting dramatically captures the biblical story of Judith beheading the Assyrian general Holofernes. The artist employs intense chiaroscuro and stark realism to highlight the gruesome and harrowing nature of the act.
items.tags: biblical, Baroque, chiaroscuro, violence, drama, realism, Old Testament

items.title: David with the Head of Goliath
items.description_narrative: This powerful painting captures the biblical hero David holding the severed head of Goliath, moments after his victory. Caravaggio's signature dramatic lighting and intense psychological realism imbue the scene with both triumph and a poignant reflection on mortality.
items.tags: biblical, baroque, chiaroscuro, religious, drama, self-portrait, oil painting, psychological

items.title: Boy with a Basket of Fruit
items.description_narrative: This early work by Caravaggio captures a youthful figure holding a bountiful basket of fruit, showcasing the artist's developing naturalistic style. The subject's soft gaze and the meticulously rendered still life elements foreshadow the dramatic realism that would define his later masterpieces.
items.tags: boy, fruit, still life, portrait, baroque, naturalism, chiaroscuro, early work

items.title: The Cardsharps
items.description_narrative: This painting vividly portrays a scene of deceit, as a naive youth is subtly cheated in a game of cards by a cunning opponent with an accomplice. Caravaggio's masterful use of dramatic lighting and intense realism brings the psychological tension of the moment to life.
items.tags: baroque, tenebrism, realism, genre painting, card game, deceit, drama

items.title: Self-Portrait as the Allegory of Painting
items.description_narrative: Artemisia Gentileschi portrays herself absorbed in the act of painting, her face partially obscured, emphasizing the intense concentration required of an artist. This powerful self-portrait serves as an allegory for painting itself, showcasing her skill and asserting her professional identity in a male-dominated art world.
items.tags: self-portrait, allegory, baroque, female artist, dramatic, painting, realism, empowering

items.title: The Garden of Love
items.description_narrative: This vibrant oil painting depicts elegantly dressed figures gathered in a lush garden, engaged in flirtatious conversation and music. Putti playfully interact with the couples and statues, embodying the themes of love and recreation prevalent in Baroque courtly life.
items.tags: baroque, flemish, garden, love, courtly life, couples, putti, festive

items.title: Samson and Delilah
items.description_narrative: Peter Paul Rubens's "Samson and Delilah" vividly captures the biblical moment of betrayal, depicting Delilah overseeing Samson's haircut as Philistine soldiers prepare to seize him. The painting is renowned for its dramatic tension, powerful figures, and rich, dynamic composition characteristic of the Baroque style.
items.tags: biblical, baroque, samson, delilah, betrayal, drama, sensuality, flemish art

items.title: The Three Graces
items.description_narrative: Peter Paul Rubens' "The Three Graces" depicts the mythological Charities, usually personifying beauty, charm, and joy. This oil painting showcases Rubens' characteristic robust and sensuous figures, embodying the opulence and dynamism of the Baroque era.
items.tags: mythological, classical, nude, baroque, flemish art, allegory, beauty, sensuous

items.title: The Surrender of Breda
items.description_narrative: Diego Velázquez's "The Surrender of Breda" depicts the key moment when Dutch governor Justinus van Nassau hands over the keys of the city to the Spanish general Ambrosio Spinola. Velázquez masterfully captures the dignity of the surrender, showcasing the magnanimity of the victors and the humanity of both sides.
items.tags: history painting, baroque, spanish golden age, military history, surrender, portraiture, spain, dutch republic

items.title: The Toilet of Venus (Rokeby Venus)
items.description_narrative: Diego Velázquez's 'The Toilet of Venus' depicts the goddess from behind, admiring her reflection in a mirror held by Cupid. This exceptional work, a rare mythological nude by the Spanish Golden Age master, challenges traditional representations of Venus.
items.tags: venus, nude, mythological, baroque, spanish golden age, reclining figure, allegory

items.title: Old Woman Frying Eggs
items.description_narrative: This early work by Velázquez depicts an elderly woman intently frying eggs over a brazier, observed by a young boy carrying a melon and a bottle. The painting masterfully uses chiaroscuro to highlight the figures and the textures of the kitchen implements, characteristic of the Spanish bodegón genre.
items.tags: spanish baroque, bodegón, genre scene, realism, chiaroscuro, kitchen, old woman, still life

items.title: The Storm on the Sea of Galilee
items.description_narrative: Rembrandt's only seascape, this dramatic oil painting captures the biblical moment when Jesus calms a raging storm on the Sea of Galilee. The turbulent waves and terrified disciples highlight the raw power of nature contrasted with divine intervention.
items.tags: biblical, seascape, storm, jesus, baroque, dutch golden age, dramatic, religious

items.title: The Penitent Magdalene
items.description_narrative: Georges de La Tour's 'The Penitent Magdalene' powerfully depicts Mary Magdalene in contemplation, illuminated by a single candle that casts deep shadows. This iconic work highlights the artist's masterful use of chiaroscuro to evoke solemn introspection and spiritual reflection.
items.tags: mary magdalene, religious, contemplation, baroque, chiaroscuro, tenebrism, solemn, spiritual

items.title: Saint Francis in Meditation
items.description_narrative: Francisco de Zurbarán's "Saint Francis in Meditation" powerfully depicts the revered saint in profound contemplation. The composition emphasizes his humble devotion through dramatic lighting and a stark, solemn atmosphere.
items.tags: religious, baroque, spanish, saint, francis, meditation, solemn, chiaroscuro

items.title: Et in Arcadia ego
items.description_narrative: Four Arcadian shepherds and a woman gather around a solemn tomb, contemplating the inscription "Et in Arcadia ego." This iconic Baroque painting explores themes of mortality and the inescapable presence of death, even in an idyllic landscape.
items.tags: classical, baroque, memento mori, allegory, pastoral, landscape, contemplation, philosophy

items.title: Seaport with the Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba
items.description_narrative: Claude Lorrain's "Seaport with the Embarkation of the Queen of Sheba" portrays a magnificent harbor scene bathed in the golden light of dawn or dusk. This iconic classical landscape is celebrated for its idealized composition, atmospheric depth, and the dramatic interplay of architectural grandeur with human figures.
items.tags: classical, landscape, baroque, seaport, biblical, atmospheric, idealized, grandeur

items.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Philip
items.description_narrative: This powerful Baroque painting depicts the dramatic martyrdom of Saint Philip, emphasizing his physical suffering and spiritual endurance. Ribera's characteristic realism and intense emotional portrayal draw the viewer into the raw brutality and profound faith of the scene.
items.tags: baroque, spanish baroque, religious art, martyrdom, violence, suffering, realism, drama

items.title: The Immaculate Conception
items.description_narrative: Bartolomé Esteban Murillo's 'The Immaculate Conception' depicts the Virgin Mary ascending amidst a heavenly host, embodying purity and divine grace. This oil on canvas masterfully conveys the theological concept through soft light, rich color, and a serene composition.
items.tags: religious art, baroque, spanish baroque, catholic, virgin mary, celestial, oil painting, spiritual

items.title: Las Meninas
items.description_narrative: Velázquez places himself at his easel alongside the young Infanta Margarita Theresa and her attendants, while the king and queen appear only as reflections in a mirror. Its layered play of viewpoints and presence has made it one of the most analyzed paintings in Western art history.
items.tags: baroque, spanish, court, portrait, illusion, masterpiece, velazquez

items.title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
items.description_narrative: Judith and her maidservant pin down the Assyrian general Holofernes as blood sprays across the sheets in an unflinchingly physical rendering of the biblical story. Gentileschi's forceful realism and command of chiaroscuro established her as one of the era's most powerful Caravaggisti.
items.tags: baroque, biblical, dramatic, chiaroscuro, violent, italian, gentileschi

items.title: The Descent from the Cross
items.description_narrative: Christ's limp body is lowered along a diagonal sweep of white cloth, its pallor set against the surrounding figures' grief-stricken faces and rich crimson drapery. The triptych's controlled emotion and sculptural clarity mark a shift toward calmer classicism within Rubens's Baroque vocabulary.
items.tags: baroque, flemish, religious, somber, triptych, antwerp, rubens

items.title: The Massacre of the Innocents
items.description_narrative: Soldiers and desperate mothers grapple in a violent tangle of bodies as Herod's men carry out the biblical slaughter of infants in Bethlehem. Rubens channels the raw physicality of Michelangelo and the color of Titian into one of the most brutal history paintings of the Baroque era.
items.tags: baroque, flemish, biblical, violent, dramatic, dynamic, rubens

items.title: Susanna and the Elders
items.description_narrative: Painted when Gentileschi was only seventeen, the composition shows Susanna recoiling in genuine distress from two leering elders, a striking departure from the eroticized treatments common to the subject. Its psychological honesty distinguishes it as one of the earliest and most incisive works by a woman in the Caravaggisti circle.
items.tags: baroque, biblical, italian, psychological, chiaroscuro, gentileschi, early work

items.title: Esther before Ahasuerus
items.description_narrative: Artemisia's largest known canvas depicts Queen Esther fainting before King Ahasuerus after breaking court protocol to plead for her people. X-rays revealed a painted-over page boy restraining a dog, a compositional link to Veronese's treatment of the theme.

items.title: The Abduction of the Sabine Women
items.description_narrative: The Metropolitan's version stages the Roman founding myth in which Romulus's men seize the Sabine women during a festival, arranged as a frieze of struggling figures. Poussin's rigorous classical composition was studied closely by later artists including Jacques-Louis David.

items.title: Agnus Dei
items.description_narrative: A single bound lamb lies on its side against a plain dark ground, a spare image of Christ as the sacrificial Lamb of God. Its sculptural realism and stark tenebrist lighting make it one of the most affecting devotional still lifes of the Spanish Baroque.

items.title: The Holy Family with Saints Elizabeth and John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: Rubens painted this intimate devotional scene not long after returning to Antwerp from Italy, combining Flemish naturalism with the grand figural style he had absorbed from Italian art. The composition gathers the Holy Family with Saint Elizabeth and the infant John the Baptist in an affectionate domestic grouping.

items.title: Salome with the Head of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: Guido Reni painted several versions of this biblical subject late in his career, presenting Salome with cool composure rather than horror as she receives the severed head of John the Baptist. The painting exemplifies the idealized classical beauty and refined technique for which Reni was renowned in Baroque Bologna.

items.title: Saint Romanus of Antioch and Saint Barulas
items.description_narrative: Zurbarán painted this depiction of the early Christian martyr Saint Romanus of Antioch alongside the child martyr Saint Barulas for a Spanish monastic commission. The painting reflects Zurbarán's characteristic austere realism and use of dramatic light to heighten devotional intensity.

items.title: Landscape with Saint John on Patmos
items.description_narrative: Nicolas Poussin's "Landscape with Saint John on Patmos" depicts the evangelist on the island of Patmos, a traditional setting for the writing of the Book of Revelation. The scene is presented as an idealized classical landscape, reflecting Poussin's characteristic approach to integrating figures within grand, structured natural environments.
items.tags: landscape, religious, classical, baroque, serene, saint john, patmos

items.title: The Feast in the House of Simon
items.description_narrative: This large canvas depicts the biblical episode in which a sinful woman anoints Christ's feet, painted late in El Greco's career with the assistance of his Toledo workshop. It reflects the artist's mature style of visionary color and dramatically elongated figures.

items.title: Saint Martin and the Beggar
items.description_narrative: This painting depicts the Roman soldier Saint Martin of Tours dividing his cloak to share with a beggar, a popular subject of Christian charity. El Greco produced this composition for a private chapel in Toledo, working in his characteristic elongated forms and dramatic light.

items.title: Saint Francis Kneeling in Meditation
items.description_narrative: El Greco painted numerous versions of Saint Francis in contemplative prayer, reflecting the Counter-Reformation's emphasis on personal spiritual devotion. This example shows the saint's characteristically elongated form and intense, mystical expression.

items.title: The Assumption of the Virgin
items.description_narrative: Painted as the central altarpiece for the church of Santo Domingo el Antiguo in Toledo, this was El Greco's first major Spanish commission and established the elongated figures and luminous color that became his signature style. It remains one of the artist's most celebrated large-scale religious paintings.

items.title: The Crucifixion
items.description_narrative: Francisco de Zurbarán's 1627 oil on canvas, 'The Crucifixion,' presents a singular, stark depiction of Christ on the cross. The painting is characterized by its dramatic use of light and shadow, emphasizing the figure's isolation and the solemnity of the moment.
items.tags: crucifixion, religious art, Spanish Baroque, realism, tenebrism, devotional, dramatic

items.title: Cupid Chastised
items.description_narrative: Bartolomeo Manfredi's "Cupid Chastised" depicts a mythological scene centered on the punishment of the god of love. Executed in oil on canvas, the work showcases the dramatic light and shadow characteristic of the artist's era.
items.tags: mythology, cupid, baroque, caravaggism, italian, oil painting, dramatic

items.title: Don Gaspar de Guzmán (1587–1645), Count-Duke of Olivares
items.description_narrative: This striking oil on canvas captures Don Gaspar de Guzmán, Count-Duke of Olivares, a prominent statesman and court favorite in 17th-century Spain. The portrait was skillfully rendered by Juan Bautista Martínez del Mazo, an artist associated with the Spanish court.
items.tags: portrait, nobleman, spanish art, baroque, 17th century, oil painting

items.title: The Jabach Family
items.description_narrative: This grand portrait depicts the Jabach family, patrons of the arts, in a setting indicative of their wealth and intellectual pursuits. Charles Le Brun, a leading artist of his time, masterfully captures the family's presence and status through rich detail and classical composition.
items.tags: family portrait, baroque, french art, 17th century, oil painting, group portrait, aristocracy

items.title: Charity
items.description_narrative: Guido Reni's "Charity" exemplifies the artist's refined Baroque style through its graceful composition and idealized figures. This oil on canvas work from around 1630 portrays the allegorical figure of Charity, often depicted nourishing or caring for children, embodying selfless love.
items.tags: charity, allegory, baroque, italian baroque, religious, devotion, figurative

items.title: Self-Portrait
items.description_narrative: This striking self-portrait by Salvator Rosa captures the artist's likeness, showcasing his characteristic intensity and a direct gaze. Painted with oil on canvas around 1647, it offers a personal glimpse into the artist's own perception of himself.
items.tags: self-portrait, baroque, italian, 17th century, oil painting, artist portrait, male portrait

items.title: Las Meninas (The Maids of Honour)
items.description_narrative: Velázquez's most celebrated work shows the Infanta Margarita Teresa surrounded by her maids of honour, with the painter at his easel and the king and queen reflected in a mirror. Painted in 1656, it hangs in the Museo del Prado and is renowned for its layered play of perspective, reality, and illusion.
items.tags: Las Meninas, Infanta Margarita, royal court, Prado, portraiture, self-portrait, mirror

items.title: Christ in the House of Martha and Mary
items.description_narrative: An early bodegón that combines a Sevillian kitchen scene in the foreground with the biblical episode of Christ visiting Martha and Mary glimpsed beyond. Painted around 1618, it is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: bodegón, kitchen scene, religious, Martha and Mary, National Gallery, early work, Seville

items.title: The Immaculate Conception
items.description_narrative: An early devotional painting depicting the Virgin Mary as the Immaculate Conception, standing on the moon beneath a luminous sky. Made around 1618-1619 during Velázquez's Seville period, it is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: Immaculate Conception, Virgin Mary, religious, National Gallery, Seville, early work, devotional

items.title: Tavern Scene with Two Men and a Girl (Peasants at the Table)
items.description_narrative: An early Sevillian bodegón showing two men and a young woman gathered around a tavern table set with food and drink. Painted around 1618-1619, this genre scene is held by the Museum of Fine Arts, Budapest.
items.tags: bodegón, tavern, genre scene, Seville, Budapest, early work, everyday life

items.title: Christ after the Flagellation Contemplated by the Christian Soul
items.description_narrative: The scourged Christ sits bound after the flagellation, observed by a child who personifies the Christian Soul beside a guardian angel. Painted around 1626-1628, it is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: religious, Christ, flagellation, Christian Soul, National Gallery, angel, devotional

items.title: The Needlewoman
items.description_narrative: An intimate, loosely finished portrait of a young woman absorbed in her sewing, her lowered face left barely resolved. Painted around 1640-1650, it is held by the National Gallery of Art, Washington.
items.tags: needlewoman, seamstress, sewing, portrait, unfinished, National Gallery of Art, intimate

items.title: Saint John the Evangelist on the Island of Patmos
items.description_narrative: An early work showing Saint John the Evangelist seated on the island of Patmos, writing the Book of Revelation as he gazes toward a heavenly vision. Painted around 1618-1619, it is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: Saint John, Evangelist, Patmos, Revelation, religious, National Gallery, early work

items.title: The Luncheon (El Almuerzo)
items.description_narrative: An early bodegón in which three figures of different ages share a modest meal at a table. Painted around 1617, this genre scene is held by the Hermitage Museum, Saint Petersburg.
items.tags: bodegón, luncheon, genre scene, Seville, Hermitage, early work, everyday life

items.title: Saint Catherine of Alexandria
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio depicts the martyr Saint Catherine kneeling beside the spiked wheel and sword associated with her legend, rendered with the stark chiaroscuro that became his signature. The work was painted in Rome for the banker Vincenzo Giustiniani and today hangs in Madrid's Thyssen-Bornemisza Museum.
items.tags: Baroque, chiaroscuro, martyrdom, Saint Catherine, Rome, Thyssen-Bornemisza

items.title: The Seven Works of Mercy
items.description_narrative: Painted for the Pio Monte della Misericordia in Naples, this altarpiece compresses all seven acts of Christian mercy into a single dramatic street scene lit by Caravaggio's characteristic tenebrism. It remains in situ above the confraternity's altar, one of the artist's most ambitious late compositions.
items.tags: Baroque, tenebrism, Naples, altarpiece, charity, religious

items.title: Martha and Mary Magdalene
items.description_narrative: Also known as 'The Conversion of the Magdalene,' the painting captures the moment Martha persuades her sister Mary to abandon vanity for a spiritual life, symbolized by the mirror between them. It is held today by the Detroit Institute of Arts.
items.tags: Baroque, conversion, Mary Magdalene, allegory, mirror, religious

items.title: Amor Vincit Omnia (Cupid as Victor)
items.description_narrative: A brazenly nude, laughing Cupid tramples the emblems of worldly achievement -- armor, music, laurel, and learning -- to illustrate the Latin motto 'Love Conquers All.' Painted for the connoisseur Vincenzo Giustiniani, it now hangs in Berlin's Gemaldegalerie.
items.tags: Baroque, Cupid, allegory, Giustiniani, Berlin, mythology

items.title: Rest on the Flight into Egypt
items.description_narrative: An angel plays the violin for the Holy Family as they pause during their journey to Egypt, one of Caravaggio's rare pastoral, non-violent religious scenes. The painting hangs in the Galleria Doria Pamphilj in Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, Holy Family, angel musician, landscape, religious

items.title: The Sacrifice of Isaac
items.description_narrative: The painting freezes the terrifying instant an angel stays Abraham's hand as he is about to slay his son Isaac at God's command. It was painted for Cardinal Maffeo Barberini and now hangs in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
items.tags: Baroque, Old Testament, Abraham, Isaac, Uffizi, religious drama

items.title: The Lute Player
items.description_narrative: A young musician surrounded by fruit, flowers, and a songbook demonstrates Caravaggio's early mastery of still life alongside figure painting. This version, one of several the artist made of the subject, belongs to the State Hermitage Museum in Saint Petersburg.
items.tags: Baroque, still life, music, Hermitage, genre painting

items.title: Saint Francis of Assisi in Ecstasy
items.description_narrative: An angel cradles a swooning Saint Francis after he receives the stigmata, rendered in soft moonlit tones unusual for Caravaggio's later dramatic style. The canvas is held by the Wadsworth Atheneum Museum of Art in Hartford, Connecticut.
items.tags: Baroque, Saint Francis, stigmata, angel, religious

items.title: Penitent Magdalene
items.description_narrative: Mary Magdalene sits alone on a low chair, her jewelry cast aside, weeping quietly in repentance rather than displaying conventional religious drama. One of Caravaggio's earliest religious subjects, it hangs in the Galleria Doria Pamphilj in Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, Mary Magdalene, repentance, early work, religious

items.title: The Fortune Teller (Louvre version)
items.description_narrative: A gypsy fortune teller reads a young dandy's palm while secretly slipping a ring from his finger, a moralizing scene on gullibility. Caravaggio painted at least two versions of this subject; this one belongs to the Musee du Louvre in Paris.
items.tags: Baroque, genre painting, deception, Louvre, secular

items.title: Madonna of the Rosary
items.description_narrative: This large altarpiece shows the Virgin and Christ Child distributing rosaries to kneeling worshippers through the intercession of Saint Dominic, one of Caravaggio's largest surviving works. It was likely painted in Naples and now hangs in Vienna's Kunsthistorisches Museum.
items.tags: Baroque, Madonna, rosary, altarpiece, Vienna, religious

items.title: The Fortune Teller (Capitoline version)
items.description_narrative: A second, later version of the popular fortune-teller subject, showing a gypsy woman charming a young man as she reads his palm. This painting, sometimes titled 'Good Luck,' is held by the Capitoline Museums in Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, genre painting, deception, Capitoline Museums, secular

items.title: Christ Crowned with Thorns
items.description_narrative: Roman soldiers force a crown of thorns onto Christ's head in a close, brutally intimate composition typical of Caravaggio's mature Roman period. The painting is held by the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna.
items.tags: Baroque, Passion of Christ, crown of thorns, Vienna, religious drama

items.title: Portrait of a Gentleman (possibly Scipione Borghese)
items.description_narrative: A somberly dressed nobleman gazes directly at the viewer in one of Caravaggio's rare formal portraits, tentatively identified as Cardinal Scipione Borghese, the artist's patron. Its attribution and sitter remain debated among scholars.
items.tags: Baroque, portraiture, Scipione Borghese, patron, Rome

items.title: Narcissus
items.description_narrative: The mythological youth Narcissus kneels transfixed by his own reflection in a dark pool, the composition split symmetrically to double his image. The canvas hangs in the Galleria Nazionale d'Arte Antica in Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, mythology, Narcissus, reflection, Rome, allegory

items.title: Boy Bitten by a Lizard
items.description_narrative: A startled youth recoils as a lizard hidden among fruit and flowers bites his finger, a vivid early example of Caravaggio's interest in captured, fleeting expression. The painting is held by the National Gallery, London.
items.tags: Baroque, genre painting, still life, National Gallery London, early work

items.title: Basket of Fruit
items.description_narrative: Considered the first pure still life in Italian painting, it depicts a simple wicker basket of fruit and leaves, some already showing decay, set against a bare background. The work belongs to the Pinacoteca Ambrosiana in Milan.
items.tags: Baroque, still life, Ambrosiana, Milan, fruit, innovation

items.title: The Beheading of Saint John the Baptist
items.description_narrative: Caravaggio's largest painting and only signed work depicts the executioner drawing his knife to finish beheading John the Baptist as Salome waits with a platter. Painted for the Knights of Malta, it remains in St. John's Co-Cathedral in Valletta.
items.tags: Baroque, Malta, martyrdom, signed work, tenebrism, religious

items.title: Death of the Virgin
items.description_narrative: The Virgin Mary lies in death surrounded by grieving apostles, painted with such unidealized realism -- reportedly using a drowned woman as a model -- that the commissioning church rejected it. The canvas is now in the Louvre, Paris.
items.tags: Baroque, Virgin Mary, realism, Louvre, controversy, religious

items.title: The Incredulity of Saint Thomas
items.description_narrative: The doubting apostle Thomas presses his finger directly into Christ's wound to confirm the Resurrection, a scene of visceral physical intimacy. The painting is held in the Sanssouci Picture Gallery in Potsdam, Germany.
items.tags: Baroque, Doubting Thomas, Resurrection, Potsdam, religious drama

items.title: Sick Bacchus
items.description_narrative: Widely read as a self-portrait, this early work shows Caravaggio himself, pale and unwell, cast as the wine god Bacchus, likely painted during his recovery from illness in a Roman hospital. It is held by the Galleria Borghese in Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, self-portrait, Bacchus, Borghese, early work

items.title: The Martyrdom of Saint Matthew
items.description_narrative: An assassin lunges at Matthew as he administers the sacraments, watched by fleeing witnesses and Caravaggio himself, who included his own likeness among the crowd. It is part of the Contarelli Chapel cycle in San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, martyrdom, San Luigi dei Francesi, Contarelli Chapel, religious

items.title: The Inspiration of Saint Matthew
items.description_narrative: An angel guides the hand of Saint Matthew as he writes his Gospel, the second version Caravaggio painted after the church rejected his first, more informal attempt. It hangs in the Contarelli Chapel of San Luigi dei Francesi, Rome.
items.tags: Baroque, Saint Matthew, angel, Contarelli Chapel, religious

items.title: Ecce Homo
items.description_narrative: Pilate presents the bound and crowned Christ to the crowd with the words 'Behold the Man,' rendered with Caravaggio's characteristic stark lighting and psychological tension. The painting is held in the Palazzo Bianco in Genoa.
items.tags: Baroque, Passion of Christ, Pilate, Genoa, religious drama

items.title: Saint John the Baptist in the Wilderness
items.description_narrative: A youthful John the Baptist reclines with a ram in a wooded landscape, one of several similar 'Saint John' compositions Caravaggio painted late in his career. This version is held by the Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art in Kansas City.
items.tags: Baroque, Saint John the Baptist, wilderness, Nelson-Atkins, religious

items.title: The Musicians
items.description_narrative: Four youths tune instruments and prepare to sing in an allegory of music, painted for Cardinal Francesco Maria del Monte during Caravaggio's early years in his household. The canvas is held by the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York.
items.tags: Baroque, music, allegory, Metropolitan Museum, group portrait

items.title: Medusa
items.description_narrative: Painted on a convex wooden shield, this work captures the Gorgon Medusa's severed head at the instant of death, her mouth open in a final scream. It was a diplomatic gift to Grand Duke Ferdinando I de' Medici and now hangs in the Uffizi Gallery, Florence.
items.tags: Baroque, Medusa, mythology, Uffizi, shield painting
